q: The binding energy of the bismuth-209 nucleus is $1640\,\text{MeV}$ and that of the calcium-40 nucleus $342\,\text{MeV}$. Which nucleus is more tightly bound?
a: Calcium-40. The strength of binding is described by the binding energy per nucleon: for bismuth $1640\,\text{MeV} : 209 \approx 7.85\,\text{MeV}$ and for calcium $342\,\text{MeV} : 40 \approx 8.55\,\text{MeV}$. The whole binding energy of bismuth is greater only because it has more nucleons.

q: Why is the mass of a hydrogen atom used in calculating the mass defect, and not the mass of a proton, when the mass of the nucleus is taken to be the mass of the atom?
a: The mass of an atom includes its $Z$ electrons. When $Z$ hydrogen atoms are used as the separate particles, they also contain $Z$ electrons, so the masses of the electrons cancel in the difference and what is left is the mass defect of the nucleus.
